Magic Items: The properties and powers of magic items are suppressed in the Emanation. Magical Travel: Teleportation and planar travel fail to work in the Emanation, whether it's the destination or the departure point. Creatures and Objects: A creature or an object summoned or created by magic temporarily winks out of existence in the Emanation, reappearing immediately once the space it occupied is no longer within the Emanation. Dispel Magic: Spells and magical effects such as Dispel Magic have no effect on the Emanation, and two Antimagic Field spells don't nullify each other.

name: Antipathy/Sympathy
components: V, S, M (either a lump of alum soaked in vinegar for the Antipathy effect or a drop of honey for the Sympathy effect)
desc: You apply a magical effect to a Huge or smaller creature or an object that you can see within range. You choose either to repel or attract creatures, and then you designate a kind of creature, such as dragons, goblins, or vampires. You also choose an intelligent creature and designate a category to which it belongs, such as a species. Antipathy: The enchantment causes creatures of the kind you designated to feel an intense urge to leave the area and avoid the target. When such a creature can see the target or comes within 60 feet of it, the creature makes a Wisdom saving throw or has the Frightened condition. The creature remains Frightened while it can see the target or is within 60 feet of it. While Frightened, the creature must use its movement to move to the nearest safe spot from which it can't see the target. Sympathy: The enchantment causes the designated creatures to feel an intense urge to approach the target. When such a creature can see the target or comes within 60 feet of it, the creature makes a Wisdom saving throw or has the Charmed condition and must use its movement to enter the area or move within reach of the target. Once it has done so, it can't willingly move away from the target. A target affected by this spell makes a new save once per day while within 60 feet of the target.

name: Befuddlement
components: V, S, M (a handful of clay, crystal, glass, or mineral spheres)
desc: You blast the mind of a creature that you can see within range. The target makes an Intelligence saving throw, taking 10d12 Psychic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. On a failed save, the target also has the following effects until it is cured (see below): the target can't take the Magic action, concentrate, or communicate intelligibly, and its Intelligence and Charisma scores become 1. The target can still identify its friends, follow them, and even protect them. At the end of every 30 days, the target repeats the save, ending the effects on a success. The effects can also be ended by the Greater Restoration, Heal, or Wish spell.

name: Clone
components: V, S, M (a diamond worth 1,000+ GP, which the spell consumes; a vessel worth 2,000+ GP that has a sealable lid and is large enough to hold a Medium creature, such as a coffin or a large urn; and the body or a piece of the body of the creature being cloned)
desc: You grow an inert duplicate of a living, Medium or smaller creature as a safeguard against death. This clone forms inside the vessel used in the casting and grows to full size and maturity after 120 days; you can also choose to have the clone be a younger version of the same creature. It remains inert and endures indefinitely while its vessel remains undisturbed. At any time after the clone matures, if the original creature dies, its soul transfers to the clone, provided that the soul is free and willing to return. The clone is physically identical to the original and has the same personality, memories, and abilities, but none of the original's equipment. The original creature's physical remains, if any, become inert and can't be revived, since the creature's soul is elsewhere.

name: Control Weather
components: V, S, M (burning incense and bits of earth and wood mixed in water)
desc: You take control of the weather within 5 miles of you for the duration. You must be outdoors to cast this spell, and it ends early if you go indoors. When you cast the spell, you change the current weather conditions, which are determined by the DM based on the climate and season. You can change precipitation, temperature, and wind. It takes 1d4 x 10 minutes for the new conditions to take effect. Once they do so, you can change the conditions again. When the spell ends, the weather gradually returns to normal. When you change the weather conditions, find a current condition on the following tables and change its stage by one, up or down. Precipitation ranges from Clear, to Light clouds, to Overcast or ground fog, to Rain/hail/snow, to Torrential rain/driving hail/blizzard. Temperature ranges from Unbearable heat, to Hot, to Warm, to Cool, to Cold, to Arctic cold. Wind ranges from Calm, to Moderate wind, to Strong wind, to Gale, to Storm.

name: Demiplane
desc: You create a shadowy door on a flat solid surface that you can see within range. The door is large enough to allow Medium creatures to pass through unhindered. When opened, the door leads to a demiplane that appears to be an empty room 30 feet in each dimension, made of wood or stone. When the spell ends, the door disappears, and any creatures or objects inside the demiplane remain trapped there, since the door also disappears from the other side. Each time you cast this spell, you can create a new demiplane or have the shadowy door connect to a demiplane you created with a previous casting of the spell. Additionally, if you know the nature and contents of a demiplane created by a casting of this spell by another creature, you can have the shadowy door connect to its demiplane instead.

name: Dominate Monster
desc: One creature you can see within range must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the Charmed condition for the duration. The target has Advantage on the save if you or your allies are fighting it. While the target is Charmed, you have a telepathic link with it as long as the two of you are on the same plane of existence. On your turn, you can use this link to issue commands to the creature (no action required), such as Attack that creature, Run over there, or Fetch that object. The creature does its best to obey on its turn. You can take a Magic action to take control of the target precisely until the end of your next turn. During this time, you can cause the creature to take only the actions you choose, and the creature takes no action unless you allow it. Each time the target takes damage, it makes a new Wisdom saving throw against the spell. On a successful save, the spell ends.
higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a 9th-level spell slot, the duration is Concentration, up to 8 hours.

name: Earthquake
components: V, S, M (a fistful of dirt, a piece of rock, and a lump of clay)
desc: You create a seismic disturbance at a point on the ground that you can see within range. For the duration, an intense tremor rips through the ground in a 100-foot-radius circle centered on that point and shakes creatures and structures in contact with the ground there. The ground there is Difficult Terrain. Each creature on the ground that is concentrating makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature's Concentration is broken. When you cast this spell and at the end of each of your turns for the duration, each creature on the ground in the area makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature has the Prone condition, and its Concentration is broken. This spell can have additional effects, depending on the terrain in the area, as determined by the DM. Fissures: A total of 1d6 fissures open in the spell's area at the end of the turn you cast it. Each is 1d10 x 10 feet deep and 10 feet wide, and it extends from one edge of the spell's area to the opposite side. A creature standing on a spot where a fissure opens must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or fall in. A creature that successfully saves moves with the fissure's edge as it opens. Structures: The tremor deals 50 Bludgeoning damage to any structure in contact with the ground in the area when you cast the spell and at the end of each of your turns until the spell ends. If a structure drops to 0 Hit Points, it collapses and potentially damages nearby creatures.

name: Glibness
desc: Until the spell ends, when you make a Charisma check, you can replace the number you roll with a 15. Additionally, no matter what you say, magic that would determine whether you are telling the truth indicates that you are being truthful.

name: Holy Aura
components: V, S, M (a reliquary worth 1,000+ GP)
desc: For the duration, sacred power radiates from you in a 30-foot Emanation and fills it with Bright Light. Each creature of your choice in the Emanation when you cast the spell (and when it enters the Emanation for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there) is affected for the duration as follows. The creature gains Advantage on all saving throws, and other creatures have Disadvantage on attack rolls against it until the spell ends. In addition, when a Fiend or an Undead hits an affected creature with a melee attack roll, the attacker makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the attacker has the Blinded condition until the spell ends.

name: Incendiary Cloud
desc: A swirling cloud of embers and roiling flame appears in a 20-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point within range. The cloud's area is Heavily Obscured. It lasts for the duration or until a strong wind (such as the one created by Gust of Wind) disperses it. When the cloud appears, each creature in it makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 10d8 Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature must also make this save when it enters the spell's area for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there. The cloud moves 10 feet directly away from you at the start of each of your turns.

name: Maze
desc: You banish a creature that you can see within range into a labyrinthine demiplane. The target remains there for the duration or until it escapes the maze. The target can take a Study action to try to escape. When it does so, it makes a DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) check. If it succeeds, it escapes, and the spell ends. A Minotaur or Goristro demon automatically succeeds on this check. When the spell ends, the target reappears in the space it left or, if that space is occupied, in the nearest unoccupied space.

name: Mind Blank
desc: Until the spell ends, one willing creature you touch has Immunity to Psychic damage and the Charmed condition. The target is also unaffected by anything that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts, and it can't be targeted by any Divination spell or perceived through magical scrying sensors. Even the Wish spell can't gather information about the target, observe it remotely, or control its mind.

name: Power Word Stun
desc: You speak a word of power that can overwhelm the mind of one creature you can see within range, leaving it dumbfounded. If the target has 150 Hit Points or fewer, it has the Stunned condition. Otherwise, the spell has no effect. The Stunned target makes a Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

name: Sunburst
components: V, S, M (a piece of sunstone)
desc: Brilliant sunlight flashes in a 60-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point you choose within range. Each creature in the Sphere makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 12d6 Radiant damage and has the Blinded condition for 1 minute. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only. A creature Blinded by this spell makes another Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. This spell's light is sunlight. In addition, the spell dispels any magical Darkness in its area, such as that created by the Darkness spell.

name: Telepathy
components: V, S, M (a pair of linked silver rings)
desc: You create a telepathic link with one willing creature with which you are familiar. The creature can be anywhere on the same plane of existence as you. The spell ends if you or the target are no longer on the same plane. Until the spell ends, you and the target can communicate telepathically through the link regardless of language. You can also share simple sensations and emotions through the link, sending the target happiness, dread, anger, or a mental image of an object or a location. Your telepathic communication is interrupted while either you or the target has the Incapacitated condition.

name: Tsunami
desc: A wall of water springs into existence at a point you can see within range. You can make the wall up to 300 feet long, 300 feet high, and 50 feet thick. The wall lasts for the duration. When the wall appears, each creature in its area makes a Strength saving throw, taking 6d10 Bludgeoning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. At the start of each of your turns after the wall appears, the wall, along with any creatures in it, moves 50 feet away from you. Any Huge or smaller creature inside the wall or whose space the wall enters when it moves must succeed on a Strength saving throw or take 5d10 Bludgeoning damage. A creature can take this damage only once per round. At the end of each turn, the wall's height is reduced by 50 feet, and the damage creatures take from the spell on later rounds is reduced by 1d10. When the wall reaches 0 feet in height, the spell ends. A creature caught in the wall can move by swimming, but the wall is so turbulent that the creature must succeed on a Strength (Athletics) check against your spell save DC to move at all. If it fails the check, it can't move. A creature that moves out of the wall falls to the ground.

name: Astral Projection
components: V, S, M (for each creature you affect with this spell, one jacinth worth 1,000+ GP and one ornately carved bar of silver worth 100+ GP, all of which the spell consumes)
desc: You and up to eight willing creatures within range project your astral bodies into the Astral Plane (the spell fails and the casting is wasted if you are already on that plane). Each target's body is left behind in a state of suspended animation; it has the Unconscious condition, doesn't need food or air, and doesn't age. Each target's astral body resembles its mortal form in almost every way, replicating its game statistics and possessions. The principal difference is the addition of a silvery cord that extends from between the shoulder blades of the astral body and trails behind it, fading to invisibility after 1 foot. This cord is the tether between the astral body and the mortal body. As long as the tether remains intact, you can find your way home. If the cord is cut—which happens only when an effect specifically states that it does—the target's soul and body are separated, killing the target instantly. Your astral form can travel through the Astral Plane and exit to another plane of existence. If you enter a new plane or return to the plane you were on when casting this spell, your body and possessions are transported along the silver cord, allowing you to reenter your body as you enter the new plane. The spell ends for a target when it takes any action to dismiss the spell. When the spell ends for a target and the silver cord is intact, the cord pulls the target's astral form back to its body, ending its state of suspended animation. If the spell ends prematurely for you, other targets remain in their astral forms and must find their own way back to their bodies, usually by dropping to 0 Hit Points.

name: Foresight
desc: You touch a willing creature and bestow a limited ability to see into the immediate future. For the duration, the target can't be Surprised and has Advantage on all D20 Tests (ability checks, attack rolls, and saving throws). Additionally, other creatures have Disadvantage on attack rolls against the target for the duration. This spell immediately ends if you cast it again before its duration ends.

name: Gate
components: V, S, M (a diamond worth 5,000+ GP)
desc: You conjure a portal linking an unoccupied space you can see within range to a precise location on a different plane of existence. The portal is a circular opening, which you can make 5 to 20 feet in diameter. You can orient the portal in any direction you choose. The portal lasts for the duration. The portal has a front and a back on each plane where it appears. Travel through the portal is possible only by moving through its front. Anything that does so is instantly transported to the other plane, appearing in the unoccupied space nearest to the portal. Deities and other planar rulers can prevent portals created by this spell from opening in their presence or anywhere within their domains. When you cast this spell, you can speak the name of a specific creature (a pseudonym, title, or nickname doesn't work). If that creature is on a plane other than the one you are on, the portal opens in the named creature's immediate vicinity and draws the creature through it to the nearest unoccupied space on your side of the portal. You gain no special power over the creature, and it is free to act as the DM deems appropriate. It might leave, attack you, or help you.

name: Imprisonment
components: V, S, M (a depiction of the target and a special component that varies according to the version of the spell you choose, worth 1,000+ GP per Hit Die of the target)
desc: You create a magical restraint to hold a creature that you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be bound by the spell; if it succeeds, it is immune to this spell if you cast it again. While affected by this spell, the target doesn't need to breathe, eat, or drink, and it doesn't age. Divination spells can't locate or perceive the target. When you cast the spell, you choose one of the following forms of imprisonment. Burial: The target is entombed far beneath the earth in a sphere of magical force just large enough to contain it. Nothing can pass through the sphere, nor can any creature teleport or use planar travel to get into or out of it. The special component is a small mithral orb. Chaining: Heavy chains, firmly rooted in the ground, hold the target in place. The target has the Restrained condition and can't be moved by any means. The special component is a fine chain of precious metal. Hedged Prison: The target is trapped in a maze-like demiplane. The special component is a miniature representation of the prison made from jade. Minimus Containment: The target shrinks to a height of 1 inch and is imprisoned inside a gemstone or similar object. The special component is a large, transparent crystal or gem. Slumber: The target falls into an unbreakable sleep. The special component consists of rare soporific herbs. To end the spell, you must take a Magic action to touch the target and speak its name and a special password established when you cast it, or someone must cast Dispel Magic on the target using a 9th-level spell slot, or a Wish spell can be used to end the imprisonment.

name: Mass Heal
desc: A flood of healing energy flows from you into injured creatures around you. You restore up to 700 Hit Points, divided as you choose among any number of creatures that you can see within range. Creatures healed by this spell are also cured of the Blinded, Deafened, and Poisoned conditions. This spell has no effect on Undead or Constructs.

name: Meteor Swarm
desc: Blazing orbs of fire plummet to the ground at four different points you can see within range. Each creature in a 40-foot-radius Sphere centered on each point you choose makes a Dexterity saving throw. The Sphere spreads around corners. A creature takes 20d6 Fire damage and 20d6 Bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature in the area of more than one fiery orb is affected only once. A creature that fails the save against this spell also has the Prone condition. The spell damages objects in the area and ignites flammable objects that aren't being worn or carried.

name: Power Word Heal
desc: A wave of healing energy washes over the creature you touch. The target regains all its Hit Points. If the creature has the Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Poisoned, or Stunned condition, the condition ends. If the creature has the Prone condition, it can use its Reaction to stand up. This spell has no effect on Undead or Constructs.

name: Power Word Kill
desc: You compel a creature that you can see within range to die. If the target has 100 Hit Points or fewer, it dies. Otherwise, the spell has no effect.

name: Prismatic Wall
desc: A shimmering, multicolored plane of light forms a vertical opaque wall—up to 90 feet long, 30 feet high, and 1 inch thick—centered on a point you can see within range. Alternatively, you can shape the wall into a globe up to 30 feet in diameter centered on a point you choose within range. The wall lasts for the duration. If you position the wall in a space occupied by a creature, the spell ends instantly without effect. The wall sheds Bright Light within 100 feet and Dim Light for an additional 100 feet. You and creatures you designate when you cast the spell can pass through and be near the wall without harm. If another creature that can see the wall moves within 20 feet of it or starts its turn there, the creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have the Blinded condition for 1 minute. The wall consists of seven layers, each with a different color. When a creature reaches into or passes through the wall, it does so one layer at a time through all the layers. Each layer forces the creature to make a Dexterity saving throw or be affected by that layer's properties: Red (10d6 Fire damage), Orange (10d6 Acid damage), Yellow (10d6 Lightning damage), Green (10d6 Poison damage), Blue (10d6 Cold damage), Indigo (Restrained, then potentially Petrified), and Violet (Blinded, then potentially transported to another plane). Each layer can be destroyed individually: the red layer is negated by Cold damage, orange by strong wind, yellow by Force damage, green by Passwall, blue by Fire damage, indigo by Daylight, and violet by Dispel Magic. Antimagic Field has no effect on the wall, and Dispel Magic can affect only the violet layer.

name: Shapechange
components: V, S, M (a jade circlet worth 1,500+ GP, which you must place on your head before you cast the spell)
desc: You shape-shift into another creature for the duration or until you take a Bonus Action to end the spell. The new form must be of a creature that has a Challenge Rating no higher than your level or Challenge Rating. The creature can be of any type and can have a Challenge Rating up to your level. You can't use this spell to become a creature that has a higher Challenge Rating than your level, and you must have seen a creature of the chosen kind at least once. You can't turn into a Construct or an Undead, and you must have seen such a creature at least once. Your game statistics are replaced by the chosen form's statistics, but you retain your creature type; Hit Points; Hit Point Dice; alignment; personality; and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores. You also retain your ability to speak and your skill and saving throw proficiencies (in addition to gaining those of the new form). If the new form has any of the same proficiencies as you, and the bonus listed in its stat block is higher than yours, use the form's bonus. You can't use any legendary actions or lair actions of the new form. You assume the Hit Points of your new form (in addition to your own), and when you revert, you return to the number of Hit Points you had before transforming. Your gear melds into the new form; you can't use it unless the form can wield it. You choose whether your equipment falls to the ground, merges into the new form, or is worn by it.

name: Storm of Vengeance
desc: A churning storm cloud forms, centered on a point you can see and spreading to a radius of 300 feet. Lightning flashes in the area, thunder booms, and strong winds roar. Each creature under the cloud (no more than 5,000 feet beneath it) when it appears must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 2d6 Thunder damage and has the Deafened condition for the duration. At the start of each of your later turns, the storm produces an additional effect on your turn. Turn 2: Acidic rain falls, dealing 1d6 Acid damage to each creature and object under the cloud. Turn 3: You call six bolts of lightning from the cloud to strike six creatures or objects of your choice beneath it. Each target makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 10d6 Lightning damage on a failed save or half as much on a success. Turn 4: Hailstones rain down, dealing 2d6 Bludgeoning damage to each creature under the cloud. Turns 5-10: Gusts and freezing rain assail the area, making it Heavily Obscured, dousing unprotected flames, and turning the ground there into Difficult Terrain. Each creature there takes 1d6 Cold damage. Ranged attacks with weapons are impossible in the area. The wind and rain count as a severe distraction for the purposes of maintaining Concentration. Finally, gusts of strong wind (ranging from 20 to 50 miles per hour) automatically disperse fog, mists, and similar effects in the area, whether mundane or magical.

name: Time Stop
desc: You briefly stop the flow of time for everyone but yourself. No time passes for other creatures, while you take 1d4 + 1 turns in a row, during which you can use actions and move as normal. This spell ends if one of the actions you use during this period, or any effects that you create during this period, affects a creature other than you or an object being worn or carried by someone other than you. In addition, the spell ends if you move to a place more than 1,000 feet from the location where you cast it.

name: True Polymorph
components: V, S, M (a drop of mercury, a dollop of gum arabic, and a wisp of smoke)
desc: Choose one creature or object that you can see within range. You transform the creature into a different creature, the creature into a nonmagical object, or the object into a creature (the object must be neither worn nor carried by another creature). The transformation lasts for the duration, or until the target dies or you take a Magic action to dismiss it. If you maintain Concentration on this spell for the entire possible duration, the transformation becomes permanent. Creature into Creature: If you turn a creature into another kind of creature, the new form can be any kind you choose whose Challenge Rating is equal to or less than the target's (or its level, if the target doesn't have a Challenge Rating). An unwilling creature makes a Wisdom saving throw to avoid the effect. The target's game statistics are replaced by the new form's statistics, but it retains its Hit Points, Hit Point Dice, and alignment. The target is limited in the actions it can perform by the nature of its new form, and it can't speak or cast spells unless the new form is capable of such actions. Object into Creature: You can turn an object into any kind of creature, as long as the creature's size isn't larger than the object's size and its Challenge Rating is 9 or lower. The creature is Friendly to you and your allies, and it acts on your turn. Creature into Object: If you turn a creature into an object, it transforms along with whatever it is wearing and carrying into that form, as long as the object's size isn't larger than the creature's size. The creature's statistics become those of the object, and the creature has no memory of time spent in this form after the spell ends and it returns to normal.

name: True Resurrection
components: V, S, M (a sprinkle of holy water and diamonds worth 25,000+ GP, which the spell consumes)
desc: You touch a creature that has been dead for no longer than 200 years and that died for any reason except old age. If the creature's soul is free and willing, the creature is restored to life with all its Hit Points. This spell closes all wounds, neutralizes any poison, cures all magical contagions and curses, and lifts any reductions to one of the creature's ability scores or its Hit Point maximum. The spell can even provide a new body if the original no longer exists, in which case you must speak the creature's name. The creature then appears in an unoccupied space you choose within 10 feet of you.

name: Weird
desc: Drawing on the deepest fears of a group of creatures, you create illusory creatures in their minds, visible only to them. Each creature in a 30-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point of your choice within range makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 10d10 Psychic damage and has the Frightened condition for the duration. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only. At the end of each of its turns, a target Frightened by this spell makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it takes 5d10 Psychic damage. On a successful save, the spell ends on that target.

name: Wish
desc: Wish is the mightiest spell a mortal creature can cast. By simply speaking aloud, you can alter the foundations of reality in accord with your desires. The basic use of this spell is to duplicate any other spell of level 8 or lower. You don't need to meet any requirements in that spell, including costly components. The spell simply takes effect. Alternatively, you can create one of the following effects. Object Creation: You create one object of up to 25,000 GP in value that isn't a magic item. The object can be no more than 300 feet in any dimension, and it appears in an unoccupied space you can see on the ground. Instant Health: You allow up to twenty creatures that you can see to regain all Hit Points, and you end all effects on them described in the Greater Restoration spell. Resilience: You grant one creature you can see Resistance to one damage type of your choice for 8 hours. Spell Negation: You cause one spell of level 8 or lower to be negated on one target. Recover Resources: You restore the expended spell slots of one creature of level 7 or lower. You might be able to achieve something beyond the scope of the above examples. State your wish to the DM as precisely as possible. The DM has great latitude in ruling what occurs in such an instance; the greater the wish, the greater the likelihood that something goes wrong. This spell might simply fail, the effect you desire might be achieved only in part, or you might suffer an unforeseen consequence. The stress of casting this spell to produce any effect other than duplicating another spell weakens you. After enduring that stress, each time you cast a spell until you finish a Long Rest, you take 1d10 Necrotic damage per level of that spell. This damage can't be reduced or prevented in any way. In addition, your Strength drops to 3 for 2d4 days if it isn't 3 or lower already. For each of those days that you spend resting and doing nothing more than light activity, your remaining recovery time decreases by 2 days. Finally, there is a 33 percent chance that you are unable to cast Wish ever again if you suffer this stress.
